lane: junction: vehicle-only junction conflicts (red light, stop sign or other sign, vehicle right of way, unsafe turn or lane use; broadside and sideswipe)

fixes.name: Red-light cameras
fixes.how_it_works: A camera photographs vehicles entering on red and the owner or driver is cited, so drivers stop rather than run the late phase.

groups.group: vehicles only | red light
groups.mechanism: Deters drivers from entering on red, which removes the broadside crash with cross traffic.
groups.target_share: Going-straight red-light share 2,670 of 2,982 people hurt and 142 of 153 KSI (pairs_within_mode); only at camera approaches, and the red-light note found 116 driver-run KSI crashes spread over 109 corners, so a citywide reach needs many sites [inference — mine]

effect.applies_to: Low: all injured people at the camera junction (Danish handbook, -15% personskader, -20% killed, -17% serious). Mid: angle crashes, injury severity (Goldenbeld 2019 meta-analysis, CMF 0.71). High: angle crashes of all severities (CMF 0.63). Rear-end crashes 0.98 (Goldenbeld) to +15% (FHWA 2005); Danish all-crash effect -2%.
effect.source: Vejdirektoratet Effekthåndbog 2023 §5.7; CMF Clearinghouse 11108 to 11112 (Goldenbeld et al. 2019, 4 stars)

groups.group: bicycle involved | red light
groups.mechanism: Same deterrence, but only where the driver ran the red; a camera cannot cite a bicyclist.
groups.target_share: 352 people hurt, 53 KSI in the group; the driver-run share is not split at this grain. The red-light note found 64 of 207 red-light KSI (2021 to Aug 2026, all modes) were run by a bike, scooter or pedestrian [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]

effect.applies_to: Injured people at camera junctions, all road users (Danish handbook); no bicycle-specific estimate found

groups.group: pedestrian involved | red light
groups.mechanism: Same deterrence where the driver ran the red; pedestrian red-runners are out of reach.
groups.target_share: 267 people hurt, 54 KSI; the red-light note counted 28 of 82 people hit by a red-running driver as pedestrians (KSI, 2021 to Aug 2026) [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]

effect.applies_to: Injured people at camera junctions, all road users

fixes.unit: per approach (one direction into an intersection)

cost.unit: per approach to build, plus about $42,000 per approach a year for the vendor; a city presenter gave $0.5M to $1M per camera
cost.source: SFMTA Citizens' Advisory Council deck, Automated Speed and Red Light Enforcement, 2026-06-04, via red-light note

fixes.sf_now: SFMTA lists 25 approaches at 18 intersections and switched on 6 new sites on 2026-11-15; citation data shows 13 intersections, so the two SFMTA sources disagree. 10,385 citations in 2025, each a $485 moving violation [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]
fixes.sf_evidence: SFMTA credits cameras, engineering and education together with a 70% citywide drop in red-light injury collisions, 1996 to 2025, a naive bundled figure. No camera-only SF evaluation found. A baseline exists for the six new sites (26 injury crashes 2023 to 2025 against 29.2 expected); three years after could show only a drop of 54% or more [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA picks sites within the surveillance policy the Board of Supervisors approved by ordinance (Ordinance 111-25); a site outside it needs another ordinance (Admin Code 19B.2(a)); the state sets the fine and liability, and SB 720 (2025) lets a city opt into $100 civil tickets [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]; SB 720 detail [secondary — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: high: several meta-analyses (Cochrane, Høye, Goldenbeld 2019) agree on fewer angle and injury crashes, with a rear-end increase that lowers the all-crash net to near zero

fixes.name: Longer all-red clearance interval
fixes.how_it_works: Adds a second or two when every approach shows red, so a driver who enters at the end of yellow clears before cross traffic gets green.

groups.group: vehicles only | red light
groups.mechanism: Gives late entrants time to clear, removing the broadside with the first cross-traffic vehicle.
groups.target_share: Going-straight red-light share 2,670 of 2,982 people hurt (pairs_within_mode); placed at signals where a street posted 35 mph or more meets, the few where approach speeds are highest (reach.json)

effect.applies_to: Low: crashes and injuries at the few Danish junctions where clearance needs adjusting (the handbook says most do not). Mid: injury crashes, CMF 0.86 (Srinivasan 2011). High: all crashes, CMF 0.80. Applied only at signals where a street posted 35 mph or more meets
effect.source: Vejdirektoratet Effekthåndbog 2023 §5.7 (about -10%); CMF Clearinghouse 4211 and 4212 via red-light note

groups.group: bicycle involved | red light
groups.mechanism: Same clearance protects a bicyclist who enters on green against a late car.
groups.target_share: 352 people hurt, 53 KSI; driver-run share not split at this grain

effect.applies_to: All crashes and injuries at adjusted junctions; no bicycle-specific value

cost.unit: per intersection; staff retiming time only, no SF figure found

fixes.sf_now: SF ran 4.0 second yellows at 25 mph against a 3.6 second state minimum in 2019; current all-red times by signal are not published [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]
fixes.sf_evidence: None: the signal inventory (DataSF ybh5-27n2) has no timing dates, so no before and after test is possible.
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA traffic signal engineers [model knowledge — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: moderate: US empirical Bayes CMFs rated 3 to 4 stars and a Danish handbook value, but the Danish authors say the gain is limited to a few junctions, so the tool places it only at signals on streets posted 35 mph or more

fixes.name: Retroreflective backplates, larger and extra signal heads, mast arms
fixes.how_it_works: Makes the signal easier to see by day and at night so fewer drivers miss the change to red.

groups.group: vehicles only | red light
groups.mechanism: Fewer unintended red-light entries by drivers who did not see the signal.
groups.target_share: 2,670 going straight of 2,982; the unintended share of red-running is unknown [inference — mine]

effect.applies_to: Low and mid: all crashes in the influence area, backplates and hardware (LRSM SI02 CRF 15%; CMF 1410). High: converting pedestal-mounted heads to mast arms (LRSM SI07 CRF 30%). The Danish handbook reports significant falls in injury crashes in darkness but gives no number
effect.source: Caltrans LRSM v1.8 Table 1, SI02 and SI07

groups.group: vehicles only | stop sign or other sign
groups.mechanism: Larger or added stop and warning signs at stop-controlled corners cut missed-stop broadsides.
groups.target_share: Going straight 989 of 1,323 people hurt, 37 of 53 KSI (size_families)

effect.applies_to: All crashes in the influence area of a non-signalized intersection (LRSM NS08)

cost.unit: per location for a full SF signal upgrade (Contract 35: $20.1M over 17 locations, including mast arms, left-turn signals, countdown and accessible signals, lighting and 97 curb ramps); backplates alone are far cheaper but no SF figure found. Per location is [inference — mine]

fixes.sf_now: Which SF signals have retroreflective backplates is not published [primary — read 2026-11-20, per red-light note]; SF is upgrading signals contract by contract (Contract 35, 17 locations, 2025)
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA, funded mostly by Prop L sales tax and GO bonds per the SFCTA release [primary — read 2026-11-25]
fixes.evidence_grade: moderate: FHWA proven countermeasure with a 4-star CMF for backplates; mast-arm and Danish dark-hour results less precise

fixes.name: Protected-only left-turn phase
fixes.how_it_works: Left-turning drivers get their own green arrow and are held on red while opposing traffic and the crosswalk they turn across have green.

groups.group: vehicles only | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Removes the gap-judging left turn across oncoming traffic at signals.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,814 of 3,119 people hurt, 89 of 121 KSI (pairs_within_mode); only the part at signals with permissive lefts, which this data does not split; 66% of intersection KSI citywide were at signals (signals_at_intersections) [inference — mine]

effect.applies_to: Mid: crashes with left-turners from the treated approach, every severity (Danish handbook §5.7, from a large Danish study and a Belgian one); the handbook says other crash types do not change. Low: all crashes in the influence area (LRSM SI06 CRF 30%). High: angle crashes, CMF 333 (0.01, 4 stars), whose after count was not reported
effect.source: Vejdirektoratet Effekthåndbog 2023 §5.7; Caltrans LRSM SI06; CMF 333

groups.group: vehicles only | unsafe turn or lane use
groups.mechanism: Same separation for left turns cited as unsafe turns at signals.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,025 of 3,974 people hurt, 46 of 208 KSI (size_families); signal share not split

effect.applies_to: Crashes with left-turners from the treated approach (Danish); all crashes in influence area (LRSM)

groups.group: bicycle involved | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Holds the left-turning driver while an oncoming bicyclist goes straight.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 308 of 516 people hurt, 19 of 35 KSI (size_families)

effect.applies_to: Low: left-turn pedestrian and bicyclist injuries after left-turn-only signals, NYC naive before and after at 34 intersections. Mid and high: Danish all left-turner crashes from the treated approach
effect.source: NYC DOT left-turn study 2016; Vejdirektoratet Effekthåndbog 2023 §5.7

cost.unit: per intersection; low where the controller and heads allow a phase change (LRSM: 'the cost would also be low', in-house work), up to a full SF signal upgrade at about $1.18M a location where new heads and mast arms are needed
cost.source: Caltrans LRSM SI06 text; SFCTA Contract 35

fixes.sf_now: SF signal upgrade contracts add left-turn signals (Contract 35, 2025); the count of SF approaches with permissive versus protected lefts is not published [unretrieved — verify]
fixes.sf_evidence: None found at the signal level; SF's signal inventory has no phasing dates.
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA signal engineering, within CA MUTCD §4D guidance that the LRSM says agencies must document [primary — read 2026-11-25]
fixes.evidence_grade: high: Danish large-sample before and after and a Belgian replication agree on about -80% for the target crashes; US CMFs agree in direction. Flashing-yellow-arrow permissive phasing is weaker and replacing protected-only with it raised left-turn crashes 3.4 times in Utah (CMF 9401)

fixes.name: Left-turn lane with a curbed channelising island
fixes.how_it_works: Gives left-turners a separate, curbed waiting space so they are out of the through lane and their path across the junction is fixed.

groups.group: vehicles only | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Calmer, better-placed left turns and fewer rear-end and turning-across-oncoming crashes.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,814 of 3,119 people hurt, 89 of 121 KSI (pairs_within_mode); only streets with room for a pocket

effect.applies_to: Mid: all crashes and injuries at urban 4-leg junctions with yield control, left-turn channelisation on the main road (Danish §5.9; urban T-junction -20%); the handbook says the effect at signals is 'considerably smaller' but cannot be separated. Low: Trafikverket left-turn pocket at a 4-leg junction, about 10% of crashes, injured and killed. High: new left-turn lane plus a new left-turn phase at a signal with neither (LRSM SI05 CRF 55%)
effect.source: Vejdirektoratet Effekthåndbog 2023 §5.9; Trafikverket 2026 Table 45; Caltrans LRSM SI05

groups.group: vehicles only | unsafe turn or lane use
groups.mechanism: Fixes the turning path so turns from the wrong lane or across the centerline become harder.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,025 of 3,974 people hurt (size_families)

effect.applies_to: All crashes at the junction (Danish, Trafikverket); LRSM NS20 left-turn lane at a non-signalized junction CRF 35%
effect.source: Vejdirektoratet §5.9; Trafikverket Table 45; Caltrans LRSM NS20

cost.unit: per intersection for SF concrete islands (Next Generation Sanchez), used here as the nearest SF unit cost for a curbed island; restriping-only pockets cost less, widening far more (LRSM: 'very low to high')
cost.source: SFCTA CAC memo Sept 2025, via traffic circles costs note

fixes.sf_now: Many SF arterials have left pockets where width allows; no citywide inventory of curbed versus painted pockets found [unretrieved — verify]
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA, with Public Works for curb work [model knowledge — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: moderate: Danish and Swedish handbook values rest on two large US studies and Nordic studies; the Danish authors say results vary widely because most studies are small, and the effect at signals is smaller

fixes.name: Hardened centerline and left-turn calming (posts, rubber bumps, slow-turn wedges)
fixes.how_it_works: Rubber or concrete bumps and posts along the centerline into the crosswalk force a squarer, slower left turn and stop drivers cutting the corner.

groups.group: vehicles only | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Slower, squarer left turns give the driver longer to see oncoming traffic and cut the impact speed.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,814 of 3,119 people hurt, 89 of 121 KSI (pairs_within_mode)

effect.unit: % change in left-turn speed or speeding share, not crashes
effect.applies_to: Low: mean left-turn speed, Washington D.C. against controls (IIHS). Mid: SF average left-turn speed at 7 sites against 4 controls (1.7 mph slower). High: SF share of left turns over 15 mph. No vehicle-only crash effect found; NYC reports pedestrian severe injuries -33% at turn-calming sites (naive)
effect.source: Hu and Cicchino 2020 (IIHS); SFMTA A Turn Toward Safety 2021; NYC DOT Turn Calming page

speed_change.source: Low: Hu and Cicchino 2020 (IIHS), mean left-turn speed at Washington D.C. sites against controls, -9.8%. Mid and high: SFMTA, A Turn Toward Safety (2021), average left-turn speed at 7 SF sites against 4 controls, 1.7 mph slower (-17%). The effect's high, the share of turns over 15 mph (-71%), is not a mean speed and is not used.

groups.group: vehicles only | unsafe turn or lane use
groups.mechanism: Physically stops drivers cutting across the double yellow while turning.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,025 of 3,974 people hurt, 46 of 208 KSI; wrong way or opposing lane another 182 people hurt (size_families)

effect.unit: % change in rate of crossing the double yellow while turning
effect.applies_to: NYC sites with treatment to the stop bar (-78.9%) and to the crosswalk (-100%); a behaviour measure, not crashes

groups.group: bicycle involved | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Slower left turns across an oncoming bicyclist.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 308 of 516 people hurt, 19 of 35 KSI

effect.applies_to: No bicycle crash effect found; missing

cost.unit: per approach, narrow-island configuration (MassDOT cut sheet, PDF not opened); no SF cost for the 2021 pilot found
cost.source: MassDOT Speed Management Cut Sheets, Centerline Hardening, as summarised by search

fixes.sf_now: SFMTA piloted left-turn calming at seven high-crash intersections with posts, small rubber bumps and paint (2021); rollout count since is unknown [unretrieved — verify]
fixes.sf_evidence: Average left-turn speed -17% (1.7 mph) and turns over 15 mph -71% against four control intersections; no crash result [primary — read 2026-11-25]
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA, as a quick-build [model knowledge — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: low: controlled speed and conflict studies in SF, D.C. and NYC, but no controlled crash study for vehicle-only crashes; LADOT's 0.54 CMF it cites is for raised medians, not this device

fixes.name: Left-turn bans and directional median openings
fixes.how_it_works: Bans the left turn at a crash corner, by sign or by a median that only allows some movements, so the conflict is moved to a safer place or a three-rights loop.

groups.group: vehicles only | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Removes the left turn across oncoming traffic at the treated corner.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,814 of 3,119 people hurt, 89 of 121 KSI; only at banned corners, and turns may shift to the next corner

effect.applies_to: All crashes in the influence area: directional median openings (LRSM SI13 and NS17 CRF 50%); access management 25% to 50% (LADOT citing LRSM 2020). No non-US handbook value found; Trafikverket's 'ögla' loop turn has no study
effect.source: Caltrans LRSM v1.8 SI13, NS17; LADOT 2024 toolbox; Trafikverket 2026

groups.group: vehicles only | unsafe turn or lane use
groups.mechanism: Removes the illegal or awkward left and U-turn where it is banned physically.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,025 of 3,974 people hurt (size_families)

effect.applies_to: All crashes in influence area (LRSM)

groups.group: bicycle involved | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: No left-turning driver to cross the oncoming bicyclist.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 308 of 516 people hurt

effect.unit: % change in left-turn pedestrian and bicyclist injuries
effect.applies_to: 51 NYC intersections, 113 to 67 injuries, naive 3 years before and after

cost.unit: per intersection, for the median the vehicle effect is measured on (LRSM SI13 and NS17, directional median openings): SF concrete islands at $19,000 to $40,000 an intersection (Sanchez, the curbed-median record) up to LADOT's 'Low' band (up to $50,000). A sign-only ban is cheaper (SF D2 study: $12,000 for a blank-out turn sign with warning signs and striping, Laguna and Bay), but no record measures a sign-only ban's effect on vehicle crashes
cost.source: SFCTA CAC memo via calming costs note (curbed-median record); LADOT 2024 cost bands; SFCTA District 2 Safety Study Table 6-1

fixes.sf_now: SF uses posted turn bans, including on Market Street where a red-light camera enforces the right-turn ban at Octavia; no inventory of banned turns found [unretrieved — verify]
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA Board, through the traffic engineering public hearing process [model knowledge — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: low: US CRFs from manuals and NYC naive before and after; diversion to nearby corners is unmeasured

fixes.name: Convert a signal or stop junction to a single-lane roundabout
fixes.how_it_works: Replaces crossing and left-turn conflicts with a slow merge around a central island, so cars meet at low speed and shallow angles.

groups.group: vehicles only | red light
groups.mechanism: With no signal there is no red to run and no high-speed broadside.
groups.target_share: Going straight 2,670 of 2,982 people hurt (pairs_within_mode); only at junctions with room for a roundabout, few in SF

effect.applies_to: Urban 4-leg signal to roundabout, Danish handbook: injury crashes -5%, injured people -15%, killed -40%, all crashes 0; urban 3-leg signal to roundabout raises injured +15%. High: LRSM CRF 79% for fatal and injury crashes, which the Danish urban figures do not support

groups.group: vehicles only | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: No left turn across oncoming traffic; everyone turns right into the circle.
groups.target_share: Left or U-turn 1,814 of 3,119 people hurt, 89 of 121 KSI

effect.applies_to: Urban 4-leg yield-controlled junction to roundabout (Danish): injury crashes -20%, injured -30%, killed -55%; urban 3-leg yield junction: injured 0, killed -25%

groups.group: vehicles only | stop sign or other sign
groups.mechanism: Replaces a stop that drivers run with a yield at low speed.
groups.target_share: Going straight 989 of 1,323 people hurt, 37 of 53 KSI

effect.applies_to: Urban yield-controlled 4-leg to roundabout (Danish); Danish handbook groups stop and yield as vigepligt

groups.group: bicycle involved | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Warning: roundabouts often worsen safety for bicyclists unless the bike path is separated outside the circle.
groups.target_share: 516 people hurt, 35 KSI; all bicycle crashes at a converted junction are exposed

effect.applies_to: Danish handbook: conversion 'often' worsens safety for cyclists, moped riders and motorcyclists; designs with bike lanes or coloured bike markings in the circle perform badly; it advises urban roundabouts only where few two-wheelers or with separated paths. No number given

cost.unit: per intersection, LADOT 'High' band ($250,000 or more); LRSM says costs are 'relatively high' and may need right of way; no SF figure found

fixes.sf_now: SF has small traffic circles (36 in SFMTA's intersection layer) but few or no full roundabouts [primary — read 2026-10-31, per traffic circles note]; full roundabouts [unretrieved — verify]
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA and Public Works; Caltrans on state routes [model knowledge — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: moderate: TØI meta-analysis of 44 evaluations and two Danish studies, but urban effects are small and one Danish study of 149 urban conversions found injury crashes up 28%; harm to bicyclists is consistent

fixes.name: Mini-roundabout or traffic circle where two local streets meet
fixes.how_it_works: A mountable central island makes drivers slow and deflect at a residential or collector corner.

groups.group: vehicles only | stop sign or other sign
groups.mechanism: Drivers who would run the stop must slow to get round the island, so broadsides are rarer and slower.
groups.target_share: Going straight 989 of 1,323 people hurt, 37 of 53 KSI; 688 of the group's 1,323 people hurt were on residential streets (family_stress)

effect.unit: % change in fatal and injury crashes
effect.applies_to: Low and mid: the Danish handbook's urban finding, that rebuilding urban junctions as mini-roundabouts or single-lane roundabouts 'most often' gives no substantial fall in crashes and injuries (§5.5, no number given, read as 0%). High: multi-vehicle KABC crashes, all-way stop to mini-roundabout, urban and suburban, CMF 0.54 (Avelar 2023, 3 stars). Other studies range from KABC CMF 1.74 (Mishra 2022, 3 stars, 35 mph+ roads) to 0.39 (two-way stop to mini-roundabout, Mishra)

groups.group: vehicles only | vehicle right of way
groups.mechanism: Same deflection at uncontrolled or yield corners.
groups.target_share: Going straight 886 of 3,119 people hurt, 20 of 121 KSI; only on local streets

effect.applies_to: Vancouver local-street circles against intersections one block away, RR 0.53 (0.44 to 0.63)
effect.source: Teschke et al. 2018, via traffic circles note

groups.group: bicycle involved | stop sign or other sign
groups.mechanism: Warning: circles raised cyclist injuries in Vancouver.
groups.target_share: 241 people hurt, 20 KSI

effect.unit: % change (RR minus 1) in cyclist-car injury crashes
effect.applies_to: Vancouver circles against nearby intersections, RR 3.4 (2.7 to 4.3); pedestrian RR 1.8
effect.source: Teschke et al. 2018, via traffic circles note

cost.unit: per circle all in, an estimate from Seattle's $20,000 to $25,000 build cost plus SF's design share; no SF circle unit cost found [inference — mine]
cost.source: Traffic circles equity and costs note

fixes.sf_now: 36 circles in SFMTA's intersection layer, no costs listed (traffic circles note)
fixes.who_decides: SFMTA traffic calming program; Fire Department review of turning paths [model knowledge — verify]
fixes.evidence_grade: low: the Danish handbook finds urban mini-roundabouts mostly give no substantial reduction, US and Vancouver studies disagree in sign, and the cyclist harm is large and consistent in Vancouver

gaps: No vehicle-only crash effect for hardened centerlines or left-turn calming; SF, D.C. and NYC measured speeds, conflicts or pedestrian injuries only.

The size_families data does not split each family by signalized against unsignalized corner, so the share of 'left or U-turn' right-of-way crashes reachable by a protected left phase (signals) against a mini-roundabout or all-way stop (unsignalized) is unknown. A cross-tab of family x movement x signal is the next query.

No SF unit costs found for: protected left-turn phase change alone, all-red retiming, backplates, hardened centerline, mini-roundabout or full roundabout, raised intersection, lighting, beacons. The only SF figures are Contract 35 signal upgrades ($1.18M a location), D2 study packages, and red-light cameras ($350k an approach).

TØI handbook online (tshandbok.no) refused connection again; Danish handbook figures cite it. SafetyCube synopses for roundabouts and signal measures, Austroads SSAF (AP-R509-16) and TfL/ATE Junction Assessment Tool were not opened by this lane; they are scoring methods, not effects, and would rank junction designs by conflict severity.

Urban roundabout effects in the Danish handbook are small or negative (signal to roundabout, urban 4-leg: injury crashes -5%), against Caltrans LRSM's 79% for fatal and injury crashes. The two disagree; the record prints both.
Mini-roundabouts at all-way stops: Mishra 2022 (KABC 1.74) and Avelar 2023 (multi-vehicle KABC 0.54) disagree in sign; SF's many all-way stops make this decisive.
Bicycle harm from roundabouts and circles (Danish handbook, Vancouver RR 3.4) means any roundabout credit to vehicle groups must net out bicycle and pedestrian groups.
Following too closely (vehicles only, 1,398 hurt) and rear-end crashes raised by red-light cameras and new signals are outside this lane but must be netted when crediting cameras and signals.
Red-light camera reach: SFMTA's two lists disagree (18 against 13 intersections), and which years each camera ran is unknown.
No evidence read for stop-sign cameras, block-the-box cameras, civil red-light penalties, junction AEB or ISA in fleets, or education campaigns alone.

No study of one-way to two-way conversion, offset (staggered) junctions or banning right turn on red against vehicle-only crashes was read; Trafikverket reports 0% to 40% for staggered junctions on rural roads.
SF's own road diet test (16 corridors, about no change) conflicts with FHWA's 0.81; corridor lane counts before and after are missing.
